source.title: My body in the brain: a neurocognitive model of body-ownership

confidence_rationale: A well-cited neurocognitive model that decomposes body-ownership into exactly the components REE posits for the self-model: a pre-existing stored body model, online multisensory integration modulated by that model, and a referral step that yields the ownership experience -- with a named cortical division of labour (right TPJ incorporeability test, S2 online body representation, posterior parietal/ventral premotor recalibration, right posterior insula subjective ownership). The model-against-internal-model-of-the-body structure is a faithful biological analogue of SD-030's self-comparator and ARC-081's stored self-slot. Held below 0.7 because it is a review/model synthesis (not a single decisive experiment), and the INV-064 ordering mapping is weak.
failure_signatures: Body-ownership requires a pre-existing stored model of the body to gate which external objects are even incorporeable; without a prior self-model there is no referral step -- this is the structural prerequisite SELF-1 (stateful z_self) must satisfy before SD-030/MECH-215 can attach, and it fails if z_self is only an instantaneous EMA snapshot.

Ownership is computed as multisensory input weighted against the internal body model; when the two conflict beyond tolerance, incorporation fails -- a comparator-with-tolerance, matching SD-030's residual gate and failing exactly where the residual exceeds threshold.

The right posterior insula carries the subjective-ownership signal; if the interoceptive partner is absent the multisensory match can occur without the felt-mine experience -- predicting a dissociation that a purely exteroceptive self-model (no MECH-214 interoceptive channel) would suffer.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Body-ownership arises from the interaction of current multisensory input with internal models of the body: a stored body model tests incorporeability (right TPJ), an online body representation is maintained (S2), hand-centred coordinates are recalibrated (posterior parietal / ventral premotor), and the subjective experience of ownership is underpinned by the right posterior insula.
mapping.ree_translation: REE's self-model is a stored z_self (the internal body model) against which incoming self-relevant signals are compared (SD-030 self-stream comparator); the stored-model-precedes-referral structure is the SELF-1 prerequisite (a stateful self before agentive prediction, MECH-215). The right-TPJ incorporeability test is the biological seat of the self/other boundary REE needs for its V5 social tier, and the right-posterior-insula ownership signal is the interoceptive partner that MECH-214 requires for self-state goal content.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a synthesis model of a body-PART ownership phenomenon, not a developmental or agentive-prediction experiment. The INV-064 tag is the weakest: the model has a LAYERED structure (stored model before integration before referral) that rhymes with INV-064's representational-prerequisite logic, but it does NOT test the E1->E2->E3 maturational-necessity claim or the prefrontal-myelination prediction. The TPJ/insula localisations are harvested as completion-set partners (proposal-first), not registered.
mapping.source_context: Human cognitive neuroscience review; rubber-hand-illusion-derived neurocognitive model with fMRI/lesion localisation.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (influential, well-cited review with explicit circuit model). Mapping fidelity good for ARC-081/SD-030/MECH-215 (the stored-model + comparator + referral decomposition is close to REE's self-model architecture) but the INV-064 mapping is loose (structural analogy, not the maturational-necessity claim). Transfer risk low-moderate: a human cortical model maps onto REE latents at the functional-role level.
